newsitem.title: DENMARK: FORECAST - Danish 1997 pay rises seen higher than EU.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Danish 1997 pay rises seen higher than EU.

text.p: Danish pay rises are likely to be on average 1.5-percentage points above those of key European Union member states in 1997, the Economy Ministry said in its latest economic survey on Tuesday.
The ministry repeated a forecast in its last October report of 4.0-percent private sector wage rises in Denmark next year, adding that it expected the same percentage rise in 1998.
"This means Denmark will see pay rises almost 0.5-percentage point higher than abroad and 1.5-percentage points higher than estimated for core EU nations," the report said.
This year Danish private sector pay rises were seen rising by 4.0 percent, while public sector wages were forecast to rise by 2.9 percent in 1996 and 2.6 percent in both 1997 and 1998.
But in a statement on her ministry's new economic forecast, Economy Minister Marianne Jelved appealed for wage restraint in the spring 1997 two-year collective wage negotiations.
"Pay in Denmark is rising at a somewhat higher level than in our most important trading partners. This could put the current account surplus and employment at risk," she said.
"The government calls upon employers and unions to negotiate pay deals which will ensure that the number of unemployment can keep falling," she added.
